newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD sale to fund infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD sale to fund infrastructure.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said that the government has decided to put 50 percent of the privatization receipts from Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) into a fund to finance infrastructure projects.
"We still have to decide how to do this. But the political decision has been taken," Kandir told a Senate committee.
Kandir said the other 50 percent of the proceeds from the sale, due to begin in April, would be used to retire public sector debt.
He said an Economic Reconstruction Fund (FRE) would be set up and run by Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES).
"Fifty percent of the resources (from the CVRD sale) will go to the FRE ... to finance economic reconstruction, principally in infrastructure," Kandir said.
Kandir said the BNDES would use the money to issue special credit lines to facilitate infrastructure investments.
"This will be restricted to Vale and not extended to other privatizations," he said.
Kandir has previously estimated the government's proceeds from its 51 percent stake in Vale to be up to $6 billion.
